read the '## Deployment changes'. is it fair to make the pr author write code that is for deployment of our application as a whole. this feels like way out of scope but would make my day as maintainer of course easier

As written, it’s too broad. “Anything deployment-related” could make authors responsible for unrelated platform or application-wide deployment work.

A fairer policy is:

> When a PR changes application configuration, runtime requirements, exposed ports, environment variables, volumes, probes, jobs, or other deployment-facing behavior, update the corresponding Kubernetes manifests under `scripts/helm/testcenter` and `values.yaml`. If no deployment change is needed, say so in the PR description.

This keeps responsibility with the PR author for changes their code requires, while avoiding a blanket expectation to maintain the entire deployment system.

is it reasonable to basically just read all agents.md files? or is it too pedantic? because there are rules included that try to enforce one specific style

It’s reasonable to read all applicable `AGENTS.md` files, but not to treat every rule as equally authoritative.

Use this precedence:

1. System/developer instructions
2. User instructions
3. More-specific `AGENTS.md` nearer the file being changed
4. Personal/global `AGENTS.md`
5. Repository-wide `AGENTS.md`

For style preferences, applicability matters. A personal preference such as “prefer single quotes” should yield to the project’s formatter, linter, existing conventions, or an explicit task requirement. It shouldn’t force unrelated code into one style.

So: read them all, but interpret them as scoped guidance rather than blindly applying every stylistic rule.
